pie: dwóh₁ kóryoh₁ h₂énti sth₂éh₁yetām. nu gʷémt ḱuh₁rós pró HréwdHt-kʷe. kʷós wiHrós h₁mé próti gʷémeti? ǵʰóstos moy déḱm̥t moréyet. ḱléwos moy méǵh₂ h₁ésti. nu bʰérǵʰonts wéwket. ḱúh₁re h₁eǵ twé próti gʷémoh₂. bʰérǵʰonts dwóh₁ ǵʰóstoh₁ úd tl̥néh₂t. dyéw me ph₂ter ḱludʰí. séǵʰos moy dh₃dʰí. nu h₃sléydʰt ḱuh₁rósyo gʷéru. bʰérǵʰonts ḱuh₁rósyo ḱérd ǵʰoysóh₁ stunédt. nu séngʷt ḱuh₁rós dʰéǵʰōm stéwdt-kʷe. bʰr̥ǵʰn̥tés kóryos méwdt gʷh₂mé-kʷe ḱuh₁rósyo kóryos h₂epó. nu bʰéret ḱuh₁rósyo gʷéru h₁pónts bʰérǵʰonts ph₂térm̥. só tósmey mléwHt. méǵh₂ toy ḱléwos h₁ésti tód-kʷe toy ḱuh₁rósyo ḱléwos h₁ésti.
english: Two troops stood opposite. Then the Strong One stepped forward and cried aloud: "Which man will step against me? My hand killed a group of ten. My fame is great." Then the High One said: "Strong One, I will step against you." The High One lifted up his two hands: "Father Sky, hear me! Give me power!" Then the spear of the Strong One went astray. The High One struck the heart of the Strong One with a javelin. Then the Strong One fell to the earth and grew cold. The troop of the High One grew joyful, and the troop of the Strong One went away. Then the High One, having seized the spear of the Strong One, carried it to the father. He said to him: "Great fame is yours, and that fame of the Strong One is yours!"

pie: swéḱuros gʷṓs pékʷet. udrós bʰérǵʰus-kʷe péh₂wr̥ péri sísdetām mélit-kʷe píph₃etām ph₃tóh₁-kʷe bʰúHtām. nu bʰérǵʰus bʰéh₂t. údre téwe ǵʰóstos h₁ln̥gʷʰrós h₁ésti trémti-kʷe téwe ḱḗr. udrós stéh₂t sékʷt-kʷe. bʰérǵʰew moy ǵʰóstos h₁ln̥gʷʰrós ne h₁ésti. h₁éǵʰs powǵéyōwos. nu stéh₂t swéḱuros h₁entér mléwHt-kʷe. údre bʰérǵʰew-kʷe mē powǵéyetom. ph₃tóh₁ h₁sth₁és. gʰóstis gʰóstipoteyey ḱéywos h₁ésti. l̥gʰtóm. nu l̥gʰtā́m. h₂usési bʰudʰtā́m udrós-kʷe bʰr̥ǵʰéwey ǵʰoysóm déh₃t déh₃t-kʷe bʰérǵʰus udrṓy dwóh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁. nu sh₂ént.
english: The father-in-law was cooking cattle. Otter and the Lofty One were sitting around the fire, and they were drinking honey, and the two became drunk. Then the Lofty One spoke: "Otter, your hand is lightweight, and your heart trembles." Otter stood up and said: "Lofty One, my hand is not lightweight. Let us two go out and fight with fists!" Then the father-in-law stood up between them and spoke: "Otter and Lofty One, do not fight with fists! You two are drunk. A guest is dear to the lord. Lie down, you two!" Then the two lay down. At dawn the two woke up, and Otter gave the Lofty One a javelin, and the Lofty One gave Otter two horses. Then they became sated.

pie: h₂ówis h₁éḱwōs-kʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: márkos déh₂n̥wi tḱéyt. h₂néres tóm ne tr̥h₂wént kʷékʷlons-kʷe Hrunépt. nu yéh₂t mélit bʰéronts dl̥h₁gʰós déh₂nu sédt-kʷe. márkos gʷémt mélit-kʷe liǵʰént. dl̥h₁gʰós tósyo káput kapyét. márkos trémt swidyét-kʷe. nu tósmey bʰéh₂t. márke mē bʰéyh₂s. twé ne moréyōh₂. márkos dl̥h₁gʰṓy h₁éwkt. nu yunégt kʷékʷlōy tóm h₁élh₂t-kʷe swóm ph₂térm̥. ph₂tḗr dʰémbʰt wéwket-kʷe. márkom térh₂us. h₂nérn̥s térh₂wesi téwe-kʷe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti.
english: A wild horse dwelt beside the river. Men could not overcome it, and it broke chariots. Then the Long One, carrying honey, was going to the river, and he sat down. The wild horse stepped up and licked the honey. The Long One was grasping its head. The horse was trembling, and it was sweating. Then the Long One spoke to it: "Horse, do not become afraid! I shall not kill you." The horse became accustomed to the Long One. Then he joined it to a chariot and drove to his father. The father was astonished and said: "You overcame the wild horse. You will overcome men, and your fame will be imperishable."

pie: úpo h₃rḗḱs deywóm wérunom sesole nú deywóm h₁yaǵeto.
english: The king approached the god Werunos to pray now to the god.

pie: wĺ̥kʷos dwóh₁ bʰréh₂tēr-kʷe bʰoydʰéh₂m dʰh₁ént. wĺ̥kʷos mléwHt. dyéw moy ph₂ter wékʷos ḱl̥nudʰí. bʰréh₂trōm gʷṓs ne stéh₂yōh₂. h₁yód tóns stéh₂yōh₂ pérkunos me stundyéh₁t. wĺ̥kʷos bʰréh₂trōm gʷṓs wésni h₂éǵroy kʷéḱt. h₁yód h₁regʷesyét tóns swóm sth₂dʰlóm h₁élh₂t. dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁ gʷṓs h₂usési h₂isḱétām. tóns tósyo sth₂dʰlóm séh₂gyetām wérh₁yetām-kʷe. wĺ̥kʷe bʰoydʰéh₂m Hrunéps. h₂éǵt. tóns ne stéh₂yom. nu nébʰōs gʷm̥sḱét stunédt-kʷe pérkunos wĺ̥kʷom ph₂wénh₁. wĺ̥kʷos séngʷt tósyo-kʷe sth₂dʰlóm h₁éwseto. gʷówes tósmōd h₁éǵʰs h₁n̥dʰént h₂éǵetām-kʷe dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁ tóns h₂éǵrom. h₁yós bʰoydʰéh₂m Hrunépti pérkunos tóm stunédti.
english: Wolf and the two brothers made a pledge. Wolf spoke: "Father Sky, listen to my word! I shall not steal the cattle of the brothers. If I steal them, may Perkʷunos strike me!" But in the spring Wolf caught sight of the brothers' cattle in the pasture. When it was growing dark, he drove them to his own stall. At dawn the two brothers were seeking the cattle. They tracked them to his stall and were saying: "Wolf, you broke the pledge." He said: "I did not steal them." Then clouds were coming, and Perkʷunos struck Wolf with fire. Wolf fell, and his stall was burning. The cattle came forth out of it, and the two brothers drove them to the pasture. Whoever breaks a pledge, Perkʷunos strikes him.

pie: h₁léwdʰerosyo dʰugh₂tḗr h₂ówins h₂éǵroy péh₂st. h₁yód h₁regʷesyét wĺ̥kʷos gʷm̥sḱét. h₂óweyes trésont. dʰugh₂tḗr dʰégʷʰont péh₂wr̥ tl̥néh₂t tóm-kʷe h₁r̥sḱét. tósyo káput h₁éwset. tr̥mónts wĺ̥kʷos h₂epó léytt. nu h₂wéyst h₁léwdʰeros wékʷos mléwHt-kʷe. dʰúgh₂ter h₂ówins h₂lékses. h₁nómn̥ toy dʰéh₁oh₂ h₁éseti-kʷe tód ḱlutóm. nu h₁opéyet dʰugh₂tréy ḱwónm̥ ḱwṓ-kʷe tā́s téh₂eh₁ ḱóm péh₂st.
english: The daughter of the Free One was guarding the sheep in the pasture. When it was growing dark, a wolf was coming. The sheep trembled in fear. The daughter lifted the burning fire and went to it. She singed its head. The wolf, trembling, went away. Then the Free One heard the word and said: "Daughter, you protected the sheep. I shall set a name upon you, and it will be famous." Then he gave the daughter a dog, and the dog was guarding them with her.

pie: ǵʰoysós h₁wésum térh₃t. h₁wésus kʷékʷlōd séngʷt ḱéyto-kʷe ǵʰémi h₁épi. tósyo bʰréh₂tēr h₁ludʰét tóm-kʷe ǵʰóstōys tl̥néh₂t. h₁wésus bʰéh₂t. bʰréh₂ter moy gʷh₂tós h₁ludʰét. méne h₁éḱwons méh₂term̥ wédʰe tósyeh₂ey-kʷe wéwketu. téwe suHnús mr̥téys ne tréset. nu mért. bʰréh₂tēr tóm méh₂term̥ kʷékʷloh₁ wéǵʰet. séh₂ tóm kʷéḱt HréwdHt-kʷe h₁ést-kʷe tósyeh₂s h₂éḱruh₂ srutéh₂. léwbʰe súHnew ǵʰémi h₁épi ḱéyth₂er. h₂éwsosm̥ ne widḗsi HéHḱuns-kʷe h₁éḱwons ne h₂éǵēsi. téwe ḱléwos ne néḱeti. nu logʰéyont tóm ph₂wéni h₁épi wérh₁t-kʷe bʰréh₂tēr h₁n̥gʷnéyey. h₁ń̥gʷney moy bʰréh₂term̥ deywóns bʰére. nu dʰégʷʰet péh₂wr̥ tóm. wiHrṓs tósyo ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos memnḗr.
english: A javelin wounded the Good One. The Good One fell from the chariot and lay upon the earth. His brother arrived and lifted him with his hands. The Good One spoke: "Brother, death has arrived for me. Lead my horses to the mother and say to her: 'Your son did not tremble before death.'" Then he died. The brother transported him by chariot to the mother. She caught sight of him and cried aloud, and her tears were flowing: "Beloved son, you lie upon the earth. You will not see the dawn, and you will not drive the swift horses. But your fame will not vanish." Then they laid him upon the fire, and the brother spoke to Fire: "Fire, carry my brother to the gods!" Then the fire burned him. Men remember his imperishable fame.

pie: ph₃tós mélit píph₃et h₂nérm̥-kʷe moréyet. bʰréh₂tēr tósmey h₁ést. bʰréh₂tēr wékʷos ḱléwt gʷʰért-kʷe tósyo ḱḗr. ne h₁édoh₂ ne-kʷe péh₃oh₂. tóm widṓh₂. nu sékʷeto ǵʰoysóm kapyónts bʰréh₂tēr tóm. ph₃tós bʰérǵʰum bʰérǵʰom gʷéh₂t supnóy-kʷe ḱéyto. bʰréh₂tēr tóm stéygʰet ḱéym̥h₁nom-kʷe ph₃tóm widét. nu HréwdHt. ph₃te bʰudʰdʰí. tósyo bʰréh₂tēr h₁ésmi h₁yóm moréyes. nu ph₃tós bʰéwdʰt stéh₂t-kʷe trémt-kʷe. nu térdt bʰréh₂tēr tósyo ḱérd ǵʰoysóh₁ ph₃tós-kʷe mért. nu mélit péh₃t méwdt-kʷe h₁ést-kʷe tósyo ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom.
english: The Drunken One was drinking honey, and he killed a man. He had a brother. The brother heard the word, and his heart grew warm: "I shall not eat, and I shall not drink. Let me find him!" Then the brother, grasping a javelin, followed him. The Drunken One had gone onto a high hill and was lying in sleep. The brother climbed it and saw the Drunken One lying. Then he cried aloud: "Drunken One, wake up! I am the brother of him whom you killed." Then the Drunken One woke up and stood up, and he was trembling. Then the brother bored through his heart with the javelin, and the Drunken One died. Then he drank honey and grew joyful, and his fame was imperishable.

pie: kóryos h₂réydʰeto. nu mléwHt lewbʰósyo méh₂tēr tósmey. súHnew moy toy dwóh₁ stóygʰoh₁ h₂énti h₁stés. h₁yód kéh₃tum wéyḱesi méresi h₁éseti-kʷe toy ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos. h₁yód téwe ph₂tréh₁ sédyēsi gʷíh₃wēsi h₂néres-kʷe téwe h₁nómn̥ ne ḱléwonti. lewbʰós h₂éǵt. méh₂ter kéh₃tum wéyḱoh₂. h₂nḗr mért. ḱléwos ne mért. nu trémt méh₂tr̥s ḱḗr. tóm h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂h₁ woséyet déh₃t-kʷe tósmey gʷéru. nu h₂éǵet lewbʰós kʷékʷlom pró. méh₂tēr bʰérǵʰoy h₁épi sth₂éh₁yet tóm-kʷe spéḱyet. gʷh₂tós lewbʰóm lémbʰt tósyo-kʷe ḱléwos ne mért.
english: The troop was making itself ready. Then the mother of the Beloved said to him: "My son, two paths are before you. If you enter the fight, you will die, and imperishable fame will be yours. If you sit with your father, you will live, and men will not hear your name." The Beloved said: "Mother, I shall enter the fight. A man dies; fame does not die." Then the mother's heart trembled. She clothed him with wool and gave him a spear. Then the Beloved drove the chariot forward. The mother stood on the hill and was looking at him. Death seized the Beloved, and his fame did not die.

pie: kéh₂ilos bʰéwdʰt. léwkt. stéh₂t h₂uséy-kʷe wérh₁t. h₂éwsos moy diwés dʰúgh₂ter wékʷos ḱludʰí. kéh₃tum h₁n̥dó h₁éymi. déḱm̥t Hyudʰsmṓs h₁mé próti sth₂éh₁yonti. téwe léwkm̥ widóyh₁m̥. h₂éwsōs tóm ḱléwt. nu wéyḱt kéh₂ilos kéh₃tum moréyet-kʷe h₁néwn̥ Hyudʰsmóns. nu h₃wáth₂t ǵʰoysós tóm. kéh₂ilos ǵʰémi h₁épi légʰyet sóh₂wl̥-kʷe séngʷt. h₁regʷesyét. nu h₂wést kéh₂ilos-kʷe tósyeh₂s léwkm̥ kʷéḱt mért-kʷe. diwés dʰugh₂tḗr HréwdHt.
english: The Hale One woke up. It grew bright. He stood up and spoke to Dawn: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, hear my word! I am going into the fight. Ten warriors are standing against me. May I see your light!" Dawn heard him. Then the Hale One entered the fight and killed nine warriors. Then a javelin wounded him. The Hale One was lying upon the earth, and the sun went down. It grew dark. Then dawn broke, and the Hale One caught sight of her light and died. The daughter of Sky cried aloud.

pie: gʷnéh₂s wiHrós kh₃téwi séngʷt. tósyeh₂s dayh₂wḗr tóm kʷékʷloh₁ wéǵʰet. gʷḗn tóm kʷéḱt HréwdHt-kʷe stunédt-kʷe swóm psténm̥. wíHre légʰyesi. sóh₂wl̥ ne spéḱyesi. wékʷos moy ne ḱléwsesi. kʷís h₁mé h₂léksēti? kʷís h₂ówins péh₂seti? dayh₂wḗr bʰéh₂t. gʷénh₂ mē bʰéyh₂s. twé h₂ówins-kʷe h₂léksōh₂. nu péh₂wr̥ démetām tóm-kʷe tósmi logʰéyetām. péh₂wr̥ tóm h₁éwset h₁éyt-kʷe tósyo bʰéh₂os dyḗm úd. dayh₂wḗr tósyo gʷéru bʰérǵʰoy h₁épi h₃réǵet sékʷt-kʷe. h₂néres tód widóyh₁ent tósyo-kʷe h₁nómn̥ memnih₁ént. tósyo ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti.
english: The woman's husband fell in the fight. Her husband's brother transported him by chariot. The woman caught sight of him and cried aloud, and she struck her own breast: "Husband, you are lying down. You do not look at the sun. You do not listen to my word. Who will protect me? Who will guard the sheep?" The husband's brother spoke: "Woman, do not become afraid! I shall protect you and the sheep." Then the two put together a fire and laid him on it. The fire burned him, and its radiance went up to the sky. The husband's brother set his spear upright on the hill and said: "May men see it, and may they remember his name! His fame will be imperishable."

pie: gʰósteyes bʰréh₂trōm swésorm̥ h₁pént wédʰont-kʷe tā́m swéh₂m bʰérǵʰm̥ h₁n̥dó. bʰérǵʰs bʰr̥ǵʰéntih₂ h₁ést tósyeh₂s-kʷe dʰéyǵʰos dl̥h₁gʰóm h₁ést. dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁ dʰéyǵʰos h₁r̥sḱétām HrudHtā́m-kʷe. swésor gʷíh₃wesi? swésōr tóh₁ h₂wéyst sékʷt-kʷe. gʷíh₃woh₂. ph₂sénti me. h₁yód h₁regʷesyét dʰéyǵʰos stéygʰetām. supnóy légʰyont. nu kʷḱtā́m bʰréh₂terh₁ swésorm̥ tā́m-kʷe spr̥tā́m. bʰr̥ǵʰés gʰóstipotis bʰéwdʰt tóh₁-kʷe sékʷeto. tóm pr̥wéni próti sth₂tā́m moréyetām-kʷe. nu snéh₂t swésōr déh₂nu bʰréh₂tr̥bʰis pér méwdt-kʷe tóysōm ph₂tḗr tóysōm-kʷe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁ésti.
english: Strangers seized the sister of the two brothers and led her into their own stronghold. The stronghold was high, and its wall was long. The two brothers went to the wall and cried aloud: "Sister, are you alive?" The sister heard them and said: "I am alive. They are guarding me." When it was growing dark, they climbed the wall. They were lying in sleep. Then the brothers caught sight of the sister and freed her. But the lord of the stronghold woke up and followed them. At the ford the two stood up against him and killed him. Then the sister swam through the river with the brothers, and their father grew joyful, and their fame is imperishable.

pie: gʰóstipotis mért. nu stoh₂éyet bʰréh₂tēr déḱm̥t gʷṓs bʰérǵʰoy h₁épi sékʷt-kʷe. h₁yós térh₂weti tósmey gʷṓs déh₃oh₂. nu yunégt swēḱurós kʷékʷlōy dwóh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ yunégt-kʷe h₁ln̥gʷʰrós kʷékʷlōy dwóh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁. nu h₂éǵetām HéHḱuns h₁éḱwons bʰérǵʰom péri. nu h₃sléydʰt swēḱurósyo h₁éḱwos tósyo-kʷe kʷékʷlos Hrumptó. swēḱurós dʰéǵʰōm ní séngʷt skérdʰetām-kʷe tósyo ǵʰóstoh₁ h₁ln̥gʷʰrós-kʷe tóm dʰégʷʰh₂t. h₁ln̥gʷʰrósyo h₁éḱwōs swidyónt h₁ludʰét-kʷe h₁ln̥gʷʰrós gʷṓs. nu bʰréh₂tēr wérh₁yet. h₁lń̥gʷʰre térh₂us. gʷṓs sl̥h₂gʷdʰí. swēḱurṓy dwóyh₁ h₂ówih₁ h₁opéyet mléwHt-kʷe. swḗḱure téwe h₁éḱwōs HéHḱewes h₁sénti. dwóyh₁ h₂ówih₁ sl̥h₂gʷdʰí h₁ln̥gʷʰrósyo-kʷe h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm bʰúHt.
english: The lord had died. Then the brother made ten cattle stand at the hill and said: "Whoever overcomes, to him I shall give the cattle." Then the brother-in-law joined two horses to a chariot, and the Light One joined two horses to a chariot. Then the two drove the swift horses around the hill. Then the horse of the brother-in-law slipped, and his chariot broke. The brother-in-law fell down onto the earth, and his hands became cut, and the Light One passed by him. The horses of the Light One were sweating, and the Light One arrived at the cattle. Then the brother said: "Light One, you overcame. Take the cattle!" He gave the brother-in-law two sheep and said: "Brother-in-law, your horses are swift. Take the two sheep!" And the name of the Light One became famous.

pie: ǵm̥rós bʰérǵʰi sth₂éh₁yet déh₂nu-kʷe spéḱyet. déh₂nu gʷm̥sḱóntn̥s gʰóstins énu widét kʷékʷlons-kʷe h₂éǵont. h₃réǵm̥ ní h₁r̥sḱét wérh₁yet-kʷe. h₃réǵ gʰósteyes kʷékʷlōys gʷm̥sḱónti. h₃rḗǵs wéwket. pr̥wéni sth₂éh₁yōmes ḱélōmesdʰh₂-kʷe. nu pr̥wéni ḱélonto. gʰósteyes pérwr̥ h₁rént wiḱént-kʷe kʷékʷlōs wódr̥. nu sth₂ént tóns-kʷe ǵʰoysṓys stundént. wódr̥ h₁rudʰéh₁t. kʷékʷlōs Hrumpn̥tó h₂ékʷeh₂i-kʷe sn̥gʷént. h₃rḗǵs tóysōm h₁éḱwons lémbʰt h₁opéyet-kʷe ǵm̥rṓy tóns sékʷt-kʷe. ǵḿ̥re bʰéwdʰes. h₁wésu toy ḱléwos h₁ésti.
english: The son-in-law was standing on the stronghold, and he was looking at the river. He saw strangers coming along the river, and they were driving chariots. He went down to the king and was saying: "King, strangers are coming with chariots." The king said: "Let us stand at the ford and hide ourselves." Then they hid themselves at the ford. The strangers arrived at the ford, and the chariots entered the water. Then they stood up and struck them with javelins. The water was red. The wheels broke, and they sank in the water. The king seized their horses and gave them to the son-in-law and said: "Son-in-law, you were awake. Good fame is yours."

pie: gʷh₂tós HHḱéwōm h₁éḱwōm gʰóstipotim sléh₂gʷt. h₁éḱwōs kʷékʷloy ḱóm sth₂éh₁yont kéh₃tum-kʷe ne wiḱént. tóysōm káputh₂ dʰéǵʰōm ní dʰh₁ént h₁ést-kʷe tóysōm h₂éḱruh₂ srutéh₂. tóns ǵʰyént ne-kʷe Hyowdʰéyonto. nu kʷéḱt dyḗws ph₂tḗr tóns wérh₁yet-kʷe. h₁éḱwōs mértis usmé ne lémbʰt mértis h₂nérn̥s lémbʰt. kéh₃tum wiḱté. gʰóstipoteys wos kʷékʷlom bʰérete. nu h₁opéyet tóybʰos séǵʰos. nu h₁éḱwōs Hyowdʰéyonto kʷékʷlom-kʷe pró wéǵʰont. tóm memnḗr.
english: Death seized the master of the swift horses. The horses were standing beside the chariot, and they did not enter the fight. They put their heads down to the earth, and their tears were flowing. They drove them on, and they did not move. Father Sky caught sight of them and spoke: "Horses, death does not seize you; death seizes men. Enter the fight! Carry your master's chariot!" Then he gave them power. The horses shook themselves and transported the chariot forward. They remember him.

pie: "kʷíd wēlh₁si?"
english: "What do you want?"

pie: h₃reǵtós pr̥wéni tḱéyt h₂mélǵt-kʷe tósyo dʰugh₂tḗr gʷṓs. nu gʰóstis h₁ludʰét ḱémh₂t-kʷe. h₃reǵtós tóm ph₂wéni sodéyet séh₂-kʷe tósmey léwh₃trom bʰéret. tósmey h₂ówim pékʷet h₁opéyet-kʷe tósmey mélit wódr̥-kʷe. só h₁édt péh₃t-kʷe. nu só wéwket. h₃réǵte moy h₁wésuh₂ dédeh₃s. deywós h₁ésmi. déḱos h₂isḱóh₂. h₃reǵtós dʰémbʰt. deywós h₂éǵt. mē bʰéyh₂s. téwe h₂óweyes h₃pusih₁ént téwe-kʷe dʰugh₂tḗr h₁wésum wiHróm ǵn̥h₃yéh₁t. nu gʷémt deywós dyḗm úd h₃pusént-kʷe h₃reǵtósyo h₂óweyes. tósyo dʰugh₂tḗr h₁wésum wiHróm wésni ǵnéh₃t tósyo-kʷe h₁wésu ḱléwos méǵh₂ bʰúHt.
english: The Upright One dwelt at the ford, and his daughter was milking the cattle. Then a guest arrived, and he was tired. The Upright One seated him at the fire, and she carried a washbasin to him. She cooked a sheep for him and gave him honey and water. He ate, and he drank. Then he said: "Upright One, you were giving me good things. I am a god. I am seeking that which is proper." The Upright One was astonished. The god said: "Do not become afraid! May your sheep increase, and may your daughter meet a good husband!" Then the god stepped up to the sky, and the sheep of the Upright One increased. In the spring his daughter met a good husband, and his good fame became great.

pie: ph₂tḗr léytt. tósyo suHnús h₂wékst Hyudʰsmós-kʷe bʰúHt Hwérdʰt-kʷe tósyo h₂yuh₁n̥téh₂i. nu h₁ludʰét ph₂tḗr kóryoh₁ Hyudʰsmós-kʷe tóm próti gʷémt. kʷís Hyúdʰsme téwe ph₂tḗr h₁ésti? ph₂tḗr moy léytt. h₂néres wérh₁yonti. néḱt. téwe ph₂tḗr h₁ésmi. twé ne bʰebʰóydʰh₂e. téwe gʷéru tl̥nh₂dʰí. nu h₂éǵt. suHnúm moy gʷʰénoh₂ suHnús-wē h₁mé gʷʰéneti. nu stundtā́m. ph₂trés gʷéru tósyo ḱérd térdt. Hyudʰsmós dʰéǵʰōm séngʷt sékʷt-kʷe. nu ǵnéh₃m̥ ph₂ter twé. nu mért. HréwdHt légʰt-kʷe tósmi ḱóm. téwe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁éseti. gʷh₂tós me sl̥h₂gʷyéh₁t.
english: The father went away. His son grew up and became a warrior, and in his youth he grew strong. Then the father arrived with a troop, and the warrior stepped against him: "Warrior, who is your father?" "My father went away. Men say: 'He vanished.'" "I am your father." "I do not trust you. Lift your spear!" Then he said: "I shall strike down my son, or my son will strike me down." Then the two struck. The father's spear bored through his heart. The warrior fell to the earth and spoke: "Now, father, I have come to know you." Then he died. He cried aloud and lay down beside him: "Your fame will be imperishable. May death seize me!"

pie: h₁regʷesyét. dwóh₁ Hyudʰsmóh₁ h₃reǵtósyo h₂éǵrom h₁ludʰétām sth₂éh₁yont-kʷe tósyo gʷówes h₂én. ḱwónes supnóy légʰyont. nu h₁l̥h₂tā́m gʷṓs h₁pónth₁ tóh₁ h₂epó. nu léwkt. h₃reǵtós bʰéwdʰt swóns-kʷe gʷṓs ne widét gʷʰért-kʷe tósyo ḱḗr. HréwdHt suHnówbʰos-kʷe wérh₁t. kʷékʷlōy HéHḱuns h₁éḱwons yungtóm. tóh₁ dwóh₁ h₂nérh₁ sékʷōmesdʰh₂ h₁yóh₁ nos gʷṓs h₂éǵetām. nu stéygʰont kʷékʷlom h₁épi h₁éḱwons-kʷe ǵʰyént. gʷṓs séh₂gyont. nu kʷḱént tóh₁ pr̥wéni. gʷṓs trésonth₁ tóh₁ sh₁tā́m h₂ékʷeh₂m-kʷe pér sn̥h₂tā́m. suHnúh₁ tóh₁ ǵʰoysṓys gʷʰn̥tā́m. nu h₂éǵet h₃reǵtós gʷṓs h₂éǵrom ḱl̥wént-kʷe wiHrṓs tósyo méǵh₂ ḱléwos. deywóybʰos h₂ówim némesi h₁opéyet.
english: It was growing dark. Two warriors arrived at the pasture of the Upright One, and there his cattle were standing. The dogs were lying in sleep. Then the two, having seized the cattle, drove them away. Then it grew light. The Upright One woke up and did not see his own cattle, and his heart grew warm. He cried aloud and spoke to the two sons: "Join the swift horses to the chariot, you two! Let us follow those two men who drove our cattle." Then they climbed onto the chariot and drove the horses on. They tracked the cattle. Then at the ford they caught sight of the two. The two, trembling in fear, let the cattle go, and they were swimming through the water. The sons struck them down with javelins. Then the Upright One drove the cattle to the pasture, and men heard of his great fame. At the place of sacrifice he gave a sheep to the gods.

pie: gʷówes h₁éḱwōs-kʷe sth₂dʰlóy h₁sént. h₁yód gʷh₂tós ph₂térm̥ sléh₂gʷt dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁ gʷṓs déretām. méǵh₂yōs wéwket. h₁éḱwōs moy h₁ésonti h₁ésonti-kʷe toy gʷówes. h₁léwdʰeros h₂éǵt. h₁éḱwōs toy ne h₁ésonti ǵʰóstom-kʷe swóm bʰréh₂term̥ próti tl̥néh₂t. nu gʷémt tóysōm méh₂tēr h₁entér mléwHt-kʷe. bʰréh₂terh₁ mē powǵéyetom. ph₂tḗr wos uh₃wé diwés spéḱyeti. méǵh₂yōs h₁éḱwons sl̥h₂gʷyéh₁t sl̥h₂gʷyéh₁t-kʷe h₁léwdʰeros gʷṓs bʰoydʰéh₂m-kʷe ph₂wéni dʰh₁ih₁tā́m. tóh₁ méh₂term̥ ḱléwsetām. bʰoydʰéh₂m dʰh₁tā́m ph₃tā́m-kʷe méh₂tēr-kʷe méwdt.
english: The cattle and horses were in the stall. When death seized the father, the two brothers were separating the cattle. The Greater said: "The horses shall be mine, and the cattle shall be yours." The Free One said: "The horses shall not be yours." And he lifted his hand against his brother. Then their mother stepped between them and spoke: "Brothers, do not fight with fists! Your father is looking at you from the sky. May the Greater take the horses, and may the Free One take the cattle, and may the two make a pledge at the fire." The two listened to the mother. They made a pledge and drank, and the mother grew joyful.

pie: h₃rḗǵs déḱm̥t yóh₁r̥h₂ mréy h₁éyt. nu h₂éǵrom h₁ludʰét. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m wésto káput-kʷe ḱélet ne-kʷe ǵn̥h₃ént wiHrṓs tóm. tósyo só ḱwṓ sth₂dʰlóy ḱéyto. ḱwṓ tóm widét tóm-kʷe ǵnéh₃t tósyo-kʷe ǵʰóstom léyǵʰt. nu ḱwṓ stéwdt. gʷénh₂m̥ gʷéh₂t. déḱm̥t h₂néres h₂én sédyont h₁dént-kʷe tósyo gʷṓs. gʷḗn tósmey sékʷt. kʷís h₁ési? téwe wiHrós h₁ésmi. h₁érm̥. séh₂ tósmey wéwket. h₁yód moy wiHrós h₁ési téwe moy ph₂trés h₁némn̥bʰos wr̥h₁dʰí. nu wérh₁t swósyo ph₂trés ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ gʷḗn-kʷe tóm ǵnéh₃t méwdt-kʷe. nu h₁épt só gʷéru moréyet-kʷe tóns déḱm̥t h₂nérn̥s. nu sédt téh₂eh₁ ḱóm tósyo-kʷe ḱléwos h₁wésu bʰúHt.
english: For ten years the king was going about on the sea. Then he arrived at the pasture. He was wearing wool, and he was covering his head, and the men did not know him. That dog of his was lying in the stall. The dog saw him and knew him, and it licked his hand. Then the dog grew cold. He went to the woman. Ten men were sitting there, and they were eating his cattle. The woman said to him: "Who are you?" "I am your husband. I have arrived." She said to him: "If you are my husband, tell me the name of your father." Then he spoke the famous name of his own father, and the woman knew him and grew joyful. Then he seized the spear and killed those ten men. Then he sat down with her, and his fame became good.

pie: wiHrós pr̥wéni sth₂éh₁yet h₁ést-kʷe tósyo h₁nómn̥ ḱwṓ. gʰósteyes tóm próti gʷm̥sḱónt déḱm̥t-kʷe moréyet pérwr̥-kʷe h₁rudʰéh₁t. nu tóm h₃wth₂ént ḱémh₂t-kʷe. wérh₁t. ne légʰoh₂. sth₂éh₁yonts h₁eǵ méroh₂. kʷékʷloy h₁épi ḱl̥nitó. nu gʷémt mértis tóm. tóm ne dʰgʷʰh₂ént trésont-kʷe. nu h₃érō gʷémt tósyo-kʷe kapwéti h₁épi sédt. nu dʰgʷʰh₂ént skindént-kʷe tósyo káput. ḱunés ḱléwos méǵh₂ h₁ésti.
english: A warrior was standing at the ford, and Dog was his name. The strangers were coming against him, and he killed a group of ten, and the ford was red. Then they wounded him, and he grew tired. He said: "I shall not lie down. Standing, I shall die." He leaned on the chariot. Then death came to him. They did not come near him, and they were trembling. Then an eagle stepped up and sat down upon his head. Then they came near and were cutting off his head. The fame of Dog is great.

pie: h₁ógʷʰis bʰérǵʰom péri ḱéyto wódr̥h₂-kʷe Hwért. dʰéǵʰōm térst h₂éndʰos-kʷe néḱt gʷówes-kʷe tr̥syónt. deywṓs pérkunōy wérh₁yont. pérkune h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰn̥dʰí. wódr̥h₂ spr̥dʰí. mélit píph₃onts pérkunos Hwérdʰt. tóm gʷéh₂t h₁ógʷʰim-kʷe stunédt. h₁ógʷʰis tóm próti stéh₂t. nu gʷʰént pérkunos h₁ógʷʰim bʰérǵʰom-kʷe bʰéydt. h₂ékʷeh₂es bʰérǵʰōd ml̥h₃ént h₁éyt-kʷe déh₂nuh₂ móri. nu h₂wérst. gʷówes ph₃ént dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe dʰéwgʰt h₂éndʰos-kʷe h₁nédʰt. deywṓs h₂ǵént. pérkune h₁yós h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰéns h₁yós h₂ékʷās spérs téwe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁ésti.
english: The serpent was lying around the hill, and it had enclosed the waters. The earth dried up, and the bloom vanished, and the cattle were thirsty. The gods said to Perkʷunos: "Perkʷunos, slay the serpent! Free the waters!" Perkʷunos, drinking honey, grew strong. He went to it and struck the serpent. The serpent stood up against him. Then Perkʷunos slew the serpent and split the hill. The waters came forth out of the hill, and the rivers were going to the sea. Then it rained. The cattle drank, and the earth was productive, and bloom came forth. The gods said: "Perkʷunos, you who slew the serpent, you who freed the waters, your fame is imperishable."

pie: h₁ln̥gʷʰrós móri pér snéh₂t. só ḱémh₂t h₂ékʷeh₂i-kʷe séngʷt trémt-kʷe tósyo ḱḗr. nu HréwdHt só diwés suHnówbʰos. diwés me suHnúh₁ spr̥tóm. gʷh₂tós moy h₂énti h₁ésti. nu ḱlutā́m tóh₁ tóm kʷékʷlōy-kʷe HéHḱuns h₁éḱwons yungtā́m. h₁éḱwōs kʷékʷlom móri upér bʰéront. nu duktā́m tóm h₂ékʷeh₂s h₁éǵʰs sodéyetām-kʷe tóm kʷékʷloy h₁én. nu wéǵʰetām tóm tósyo ph₂térm̥. tóm kʷéḱt méwdt-kʷe. tóybʰos déḱm̥t h₁éḱwons h₁opéyet tóysōm-kʷe ḱléwos méǵh₂ bʰúHt.
english: The Light One was swimming through the sea. He grew tired and sank in the water, and his heart was trembling. Then he cried out to the two sons of Sky: "Sons of Sky, rescue me! Death is in front of me." Then the two heard him, and they joined swift horses to the chariot. The horses carried the chariot over the sea. Then the two drew him out of the water and seated him in the chariot. Then they transported him to his father. He caught sight of him and grew joyful. He gave the two ten horses, and their fame became great.

pie: Hyudʰsmṓs h₃réǵm̥ péri sédyont. gʷṓs gʷénh₂m̥-kʷe h₁pént. nu bʰéh₂t h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr. séh₂ moy gʷḗn h₁éseti. nu h₁léwdʰeros stéh₂t h₂éǵt-kʷe. h₃réǵ tā́m méne gʷréwh₁ h₁épm̥. séh₂ toy ne h₁éseti. h₃rḗǵs tóybʰos wéwket. tā́m gʷénh₂m̥ h₁pté. nu tā́m lm̥bʰént wédʰont-kʷe tā́m tóm. nu léytt h₁léwdʰeros swóm kʷékʷlom h₂epó mréy-kʷe sédt tósyo-kʷe h₂éḱruh₂ srutéh₂ h₁ést. wékʷos h₂én wérh₁t. h₁uséwōm dh₃tréy kéh₃tum ne wéyḱoh₂. tósyo Hyudʰsmṓs sn̥gʷih₁ént. nu h₁ést kéh₃tus méǵh₂s studént-kʷe. h₁léwdʰeros kʷékʷloy sédyet gʷéru-kʷe ne tl̥néh₂t.
english: The warriors were sitting around the king. They had seized cattle and a woman. Then the giver of good things spoke: "This woman shall be mine." Then the Free One stood up and said: "King, I seized her with my spear. She shall not be yours." The king said to them: "Seize this woman!" Then they took her and led her to him. Then the Free One went away to his own chariot and sat down by the sea, and his tears were flowing. There he spoke a word: "I shall not enter the fight for the giver of good things. May his warriors fall!" Then the fight was great, and they grew cold. But the Free One was sitting at the chariot and did not lift his spear.

pie: kéh₂ilos sh₂wéns kʷékʷlom wéydset. sh₂wéns stóygʰom énu h₁éyt. yóh₁r̥ stéygʰet bʰindn̥tó-kʷe tósyo h₃nógʰes. h₂ékʷās pér snéh₂t bʰérǵʰons-kʷe stéygʰet. nu móri h₁ért. sóh₂wl̥ wédn̥s h₂én mélh₃t. sh₂wéns kʷékʷlos dʰégʷʰet tósyo-kʷe léwks méǵh₂ih₂ h₁ést. kéh₂ilos dʰémbʰt sh₂wéney-kʷe wérh₁t. sóh₂wl̥ moy ph₂tḗr kúdʰe h₁ésti? sóh₂wl̥ wéwket. só deywṓys ḱóm h₁ésti. mélit péh₃t tetórpe-kʷe. téwe méh₂term̥ h₁idʰí. h₁yód méresi tóm widḗsi. nu h₁ludʰét kéh₂ilos tā́m sékʷt-kʷe tósyeh₂ey sh₂wéns wékʷos méh₂tr̥s-kʷe ḱḗr gʷʰért.
english: The Hale One wanted to see the wheel of the sun. He was going along the path of the sun. For a year he was walking, and his nails split. He swam through waters and climbed hills. Then he arrived at the sea. There the sun came forth out of the water. The wheel of the sun was burning, and its light was great. The Hale One was astonished and spoke to the sun: "Sun, where is my father?" The sun said: "He is with the gods. He drank honey, and he is satisfied. Go to your mother! When you die, you will see him." The Hale One arrived at her and told her the word of the sun, and the mother's heart grew warm.

pie: HéHḱus Hyudʰsmós swósyo ph₂trés gʷṓs h₂isḱét. nu h₁ludʰét só méǵh₂ déh₂nu. déh₂nu pléh₁yos h₁ést stéwdt-kʷe tósyo h₂ékʷeh₂ tósyo-kʷe h₁éḱwōs tr̥mént. nu tósmey wérh₁t. déh₂nu moy stóygʰom dh₃dʰí. ǵʰutóm toy mélit dédeh₃oh₂. nu dʰéh₁t mélit wódr̥ h₁n̥dó. déh₂nu ḱrémh₂t pérwr̥-kʷe widét. h₁éḱwons pérwr̥ pér wédʰet. gʷówes h₂én h₁dént. nu h₂éǵet gʷṓs pérwr̥ pér ph₂térm̥-kʷe h₁ludʰét. méwdt sékʷt-kʷe. léwbʰe toy ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁oh₂ h₁éseti-kʷe téwe ḱléwos méǵh₂.
english: The swift warrior was seeking the cattle of his own father. Then he arrived at a great river. The river was full, and its water had become cold, and his horses were trembling. Then he spoke to it: "River, give me a path! I shall give you poured honey." Then he put the honey into the water. The river grew slack, and he found the ford. He led the horses through the ford. On the other side the cattle were eating. Then he drove the cattle through the ford and came to the father. He grew joyful and said: "Beloved one, I shall set a famous name upon you, and your fame will be great."
